end.summary:
Discussed Bishnoi traditions, sacred groves and the Chipko movement.
Explained that tree roots hold soil and help keep water clean.
Identified tree planting and watering as ways people can protect nature.
The idea that only governments can protect nature was raised and remained partly unresolved.
end.parentNote: Asha practised examples of traditional nature-protection practices with Dev. Dev explained that roots hold soil and connected forests near springs with clean water, and they named the Bishnoi community and Chipko movement. Dev mixed up whether ordinary people can protect nature; they later said people can water trees and mentioned Amrita Devi, but this idea was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Dev to name one community practice and one way it protects plants, animals, water or soil.
